chapter: Second session: boyhood, brothers and early road years
title: How integrated Los Angeles was around 1900
summary: Spikes says early Central Avenue and Los Angeles were not segregated, with Black families living near Italians and whites in many parts of town.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: You mentioned that in Texas, the neighborhood you lived in was pretty much an integrated one. Is that right?
And how about in Los Angeles? Was there segregation residentially, or...?
Because I...I don't know. I've heard that Central Avenue was rather well-integrated in the early days. Is that right?
It wasn't just a Black section?

Oh, no, and it wasn't out after you passed... oh, about Sixth or Seventh Street, you know, wasn't anybody hardly. See, the Negroes...a lot of Negroes in those days lived around First Street--First and San Pedro and First and Central Avenue and around Third and...uh, I can't think of that name over there...oh, Hewitt, and around Fifth and Gladys and Sixth and Gladys, where it's all Skid Row now--there's quite a few Negroes lived in there, and there was a bunch lived out in Temple District--called Pitney's Flat--and that's where we lived when we first came here, for a few weeks.
But there was not like a Negro Section of town...

Well these, you know, they just like anybody else. When one or two families move in here, the next one come along want to be near them, and that's where they get segregated. Yeah, but there wasn't no particular neighborhood. They lived all over town, and uh, we lived there at Fourth and Central, and we lived next door to a colored family, and then on the other side, it was Italians and white people all down through there.

Well, since you've been in Los Angeles for so long, when did Los Angeles become segregated? When did it get to the point--and how did it get to the point where certain groups could not live on...on..after a certain street or in certain neighborhoods?
